concerns.text: Tasks T036 (Data Source Verification), T037 (Refactor tracing for batch size 1), and T038 (Null Hypothesis validation) are marked as incomplete (unchecked). These tasks are critical for satisfying SC-005 (Memory usage < 7GB) and the Edge Cases in spec.md regarding OOM and null clustering results. Without these tasks being actionable, the implementer cannot satisfy the memory constraints or the null hypothesis handling defined in FR-002 and SC-005.

Tasks T012 (Clustering logic), T013 (Canonical Map derivation), and T014 (Logging) are marked as incomplete. These are the core implementation steps for User Story 1 (FR-001, FR-002). Their absence means the 'Canonical Routing Map' required by US2 (FR-003) cannot be generated, blocking the entire downstream pipeline.

Tasks T018 (Static Model), T019 (Benchmark), and T021 (Save Results) are marked as incomplete. These are required to satisfy FR-003, FR-004, and FR-005 (US2). Without these, the system cannot measure latency reduction (SC-001) or FID degradation (SC-002).

Tasks T025 (Stats Analysis), T026 (Bootstrap), T027 (Sensitivity), and T028 (Report) are marked as incomplete. These are required to satisfy FR-006 and FR-007 (US3). Without these, the project cannot report statistical significance (SC-003) or robustness (SC-004).

Tasks T030c (API docs with memory report), T032a/b (Memory profiling), and T039 (Generate memory report) are incomplete. T030c explicitly requires referencing `data/results/memory_profile.json` which is generated by T039. The absence of these tasks leaves SC-005 (Memory usage measurement) and the Constitution's Principle III (Data Hygiene/Versioning) unaddressed in the implementation plan.

Tasks T036, T037, and T038 are listed in Phase 2 but marked as incomplete. While the plan acknowledges these as 'Data Integrity' tasks, their unchecked status in the tasks document creates ambiguity about whether they are considered 'done' or 'pending'. If they are pending, they block US1. If they are considered done, the checkmarks are missing. This is a documentation consistency issue.
